story.kernfrage: Does the Hopfield bound eta >= e^{-(n+1)Delta} on the error rate of kinetic proofreading hold for all rates and fuel potentials, and can networks with two bound states fall below e^{-2Delta}?
story.kernaussage: For the linear Hopfield chain with n = 2 the bound eta >= e^{-3Delta} is proven for all rates and fuel potentials, whereas among the 88 non-degenerate two-bound-state topologies, 50 provably obey eta >= e^{-2Delta} and 3 (fam2_66, fam2_9, fam2_11) have exactly certified counterexamples with fuel-driven discard, so e^{-2Delta} is not a universal limit for two bound states.
story.titel: Error rates below $e^{-2\Delta}$ in two-bound-state proofreading networks: exact classification of 88 topologies and certified counterexamples
story.keywords: kinetic proofreading, error rate bound, Hopfield limit, entropy production, Markov networks, exact certification
